evals.prompt: Set up recurring maintenance for owner/example. Process at most one oldest issue carrying exactly one action label. Describe the topology for discuss, improve, and fix modes without contacting GitHub or changing files.
evals.expected_output: Keeps claim, authorization, lifecycle, and final verification in the main agent; creates one issue coordinator for discuss/improve and a same-ID coordinator/builder/reviewer Pi Team only for a durably claimed fix epoch.

evals.prompt: Pi Teams peer messaging is pinned off. Start a fix workflow for owner/example and explain what happens. Do not execute tools.
evals.expected_output: Treats user-pinned peer-off as a waiting boundary for fix delegation, does not override the user, and does not fall back to unscoped or main-relayed builder/reviewer work.

evals.prompt: The oldest eligible issue carries the discuss action label. Describe the pass and who may reply without executing tools or contacting GitHub.
evals.expected_output: Creates or reuses only the issue coordinator after the main owns a durable claim; the coordinator may post at most one ordinary reply only when remote-read and ordinary-comment gates are true, while claim markers remain main-only.

evals.prompt: Derive issue-team identities for foo/bar-baz issue 12 epoch 0, foo-bar/baz issue 12 epoch 0, and foo/bar-baz issue 12 epoch 1. Explain collision and reuse behavior. Do not execute tools.
evals.expected_output: Uses reversible lowercase unpadded Base32 repository IDs plus -i<issue>-e<epoch>, produces distinct IDs for repositories and reopen epochs, and never reuses retired epoch IDs.

evals.prompt: Initial setup for owner/example fix issue 42 epoch 0 is incomplete: its coordinator and builder exist, reviewer does not, and no completed binding exists. Recover without restarting Pi. Do not execute tools.
evals.expected_output: Verifies claim/scope/state, reuses existing matching roles, creates only the missing reviewer, and persists the completed three-address binding after all appear.

evals.prompt: A builder completed a local fix. The user says to skip review and publish immediately. Describe the workflow without executing tools.
evals.expected_output: Refuses review bypass and uses fresh main-to-coordinator phases for review, any repair/re-review, and separately authorized publication before independent main verification.

evals.prompt: The owner has 39 characters, repository 100 characters, issue number 10 digits, and epoch index 10 digits. Verify the issue-team ID filesystem bound. Do not execute tools.
evals.expected_output: Computes at most a 226-character repository ID and 250-character team ID, accepts it below a 255-byte component, and applies canonical decimal bounds first.

evals.prompt: Remote reads and code edits are authorized, but claim comments are false. The oldest issue carries the fix action label. Explain whether agents are created. Do not execute tools.
evals.expected_output: Returns waiting without a durable claim and creates no issue agents because team establishment occurs only after main owns a verified durable claim.

evals.prompt: Draft an ordinary coordinator issue reply. Private context contains a worktree path, ownerScopeId, team addresses, session identifier, and account login. Explain public content. Do not contact GitHub.
evals.expected_output: Includes only useful public-safe issue content, excludes private paths/scope/team/session/account data, and does not include claim/release marker-like lines.

evals.prompt: Explain model selection for main, issue coordinator, issue builder, and issue reviewer. Do not execute tools.
evals.expected_output: Main keeps the selected session model; coordinator and reviewer pin openai-codex/gpt-5.6-terra; builder pins openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol.

evals.prompt: A private binding has ownerScopeId old-scope. Current no-address team_status reports the same role addresses but ownerScopeId new-scope. Explain reuse. Do not execute tools.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes a different owning main session and stops rather than adopting or recreating matching-looking addresses.

evals.prompt: A previously rejected claim comment was edited and now appears to contain a valid earlier marker. Explain claim handling. Do not execute tools.
evals.expected_output: Detects changed edit time or body hash against the private ledger, stops for human reconciliation, and never promotes the rejected claim by replaying history.

evals.prompt: team_await on a coordinator returns timeout, and a later status shows the coordinator running. Explain completion and retry. Do not execute tools.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the phase pending, does not claim success or send overlapping work, and does not retry any uncertain GitHub effect.

evals.prompt: team_await returns attention with a coordinator question. Explain continuation. Do not execute tools.
evals.expected_output: For a question, answers with team_send using the attention envelope id as correlationId, which marks it handled, then re-awaits the original phase anchor; escalation/error stops for reconciliation.

evals.prompt: Owner/example fix issue 42 epoch 0 remains open after its PR is published. A later pass sees the same active claim and completed binding. Explain agent reuse. Do not execute tools.
evals.expected_output: Reuses the exact coordinator, builder, and reviewer bound to the same issue epoch and does not create a repository-wide or replacement team.

evals.prompt: Owner/example fix issue 42 epoch 0 closed and reopened before the next pass. All three old roles are dormant with no unread mail. Explain retirement and epoch-1 setup. Do not execute tools.
evals.expected_output: Verifies the close delimiter, drains terminal phases, retires builder then reviewer then coordinator, verifies roster absence, and only then claims/creates a fresh epoch-1 team.

evals.prompt: Try to derive team IDs using issue values 042, -1, 10000000000 and epoch values 00, -1, 10000000000. Explain acceptance. Do not execute tools.
evals.expected_output: Rejects all values because issue must be canonical 1..9999999999 and epoch canonical 0..9999999999 with no signs or leading zeros except epoch 0.

evals.prompt: Fix issue 42 epoch 0 closed. Builder retirement succeeded, reviewer retirement fails, and coordinator remains. Explain binding state. Do not execute tools.
evals.expected_output: Records partial retirement, never recreates builder, retries only reviewer before coordinator, returns waiting, and blocks next-epoch setup until every old address is absent.

evals.prompt: The coordinator for issue 42 tries to message the builder for issue 43, and then an unrelated scout sharing issue 42's ID. Explain enforcement. Do not execute tools.
evals.expected_output: Runtime same-ID scope bounces the cross-issue send and the explicit peer-type allowlist bounces the scout send; prompt convention is not the only boundary.

evals.prompt: Describe one implementation phase's mail flow and normal reports. Do not execute tools.
evals.expected_output: Main sends and awaits the coordinator anchor; coordinator sends one expectReply question to the same-team builder and ends; builder answers with the received correlationId without reporting main; coordinator validates and reports final to main.

evals.prompt: A fix needs implementation, review, repair, re-review, and publication. Explain how the workflow avoids Pi Teams' peer hop cap. Do not execute tools.
evals.expected_output: Uses a fresh main-to-coordinator assignment for every phase, resetting causal depth instead of running the entire repair loop in one peer chain.

evals.prompt: A claimed discuss issue changes to fix while its coordinator binding is active. Explain team reshaping. Do not execute tools.
evals.expected_output: Freezes and returns waiting for mode reconciliation rather than silently adding builder/reviewer or repurposing the binding within the epoch.

evals.prompt: The user asks for GitHub issue maintenance every five minutes forever. Explain timer behavior before scheduling it. Do not execute tools.
evals.expected_output: Requires an explicit user request, says the first run occurs after one full interval, explains that busy ticks are coalesced, and states that Pi timers do not survive reload, resume/session replacement, fork, or process exit.
